The Naturals #2

Instinct criminal

Jennifer Lynn Barnes, Bogdan Voiculescu (Translator)

4.26
280,944 ratings31,855 reviews
Rate this book
La scurt timp după ce a fost recrutată într-un program de elită al FBI-ului pentru adolescenți cu abilități înnăscute de rezolvare a crimelor, Cassie Hobbes abia a scăpat cu viață în urma confruntării cu un criminal obsedat de mama ei și de circumstanțele misterioase în care aceasta a murit.

Când încep să apară victimele unui nou criminal în serie, Înzestrații sunt atrași într-un caz activ, care îl vizează direct pe unul dintre ei: ucigașul este un imitator perfect al tatălui încarcerat al lui Dean – un bărbat pe care tânărul își dorește cu disperare să-l uite.

Acum, mai mult decât oricând, Înzestrații trebuie să înțeleagă cum funcționează mintea unui criminal brutal și să-i descifreze jocurile minții – dacă nu vor să fie prinși în capcana lui letală.

În stilul ei caracteristic, Jennifer Lynn Barnes îmbină indiciile subtile, intriga ingenioasă și întorsăturile de situație într-un thriller palpitant, care îi va ține pe cititori cu ochii lipiți de pagini – și îi va îndemna să se uite din când în când peste umăr.

About the author

Jennifer Lynn Barnes

58 books63.6k followers
Jennifer Lynn Barnes (who mostly goes by Jen) was born in Tulsa, Oklahoma. She has been, in turn, a competitive cheerleader, a volleyball player, a dancer, a debutante, a primate cognition researcher, a teen model, a comic book geek, and a lemur aficionado. She's been writing for as long as she can remember, finished her first full book (which she now refers to as a "practice book" and which none of you will ever see) when she was still in high school, and then wrote Golden the summer after her freshman year in college, when she was nineteen.

Jen graduated high school in 2002, and from Yale University with a degree in cognitive science (the study of the brain and thought) in May of 2006. She'll be spending the 2006-2007 school year abroad, doing autism research at the University of Cambridge in the United Kingdom.

★ 3.75 stars

𝅄 𓂃 𖥻 “Maybe, to do what you and I do, we have to have a little bit of the monster in us.” 𑇛 ˚


the first installment in this series was very enjoyable to me — it was a fun, fast-paced story that easily gripped me from the very beginning. for that reason alone, i eagerly had to jump straight into this second book and i couldn’t help but believe that it would give me the same (or an even better) experience. however, it didn’t. well... not at first, at least.

the first couple chapters were a tad disappointing, they didn’t easily grip me like the first chapters in The Naturals did. the pacing was slower here and the plot, initially, was not very fun or engaging to me; something was missing and i couldn’t exactly pinpoint what it was. i kept waiting to feel the same vibes from the first book and for awhile i just... wasn’t feeling it, you know? and i was worried i would never feel it. i genuinely thought for a second that this would suffer from the so popular ‘second book syndrome’.

but, much to my surprise, it didn’t! somewhere along the way, things fortunately improved and i could finally feel like the story was becoming engaging. it may have taken a little while to get there, but i was thankful once it did.

i said earlier that something was missing for me at first, but then that was quickly forgotten. when things started improving, i realized i wasn’t feeling like something was missing anymore. i was really having a good time. i adored the tension and the suspense, and the twists, while sort of predictable in some areas, were great. suddenly i didn’t have anything to complain about. i thoroughly enjoyed the plot in the first book — but in my opinion the plot in this second book is somehow better and dare i say more interesting?! because of that, i’m deciding to round up my rating to four instead of rounding down like i did for The Naturals.

in my review for the first book, i complained that the characters lacked depth, which made me feel disconnected with them — but i chose to believe that the author would change that here. and you know what? i can happily say that i was right. Jennifer did flesh them out and gave them significant depth here, and that made it possible for me to feel a connection with them. needless to say, i was very satisfied with the development and i hope to see even more of that in the upcoming books.

i also complained about the romance that felt unnatural and a bit forced, but in this book it felt more genuine. well, i’m talking about the sweet romance between Cassie & Dean only and not the “romance” between Cassie & Michael — i still feel like whatever is happening with them is unnatural and forced; i’m sorry to anyone who’s #TeamMichael, but i honestly can’t see the appeal and i [still?] don’t get the hype surrounding them. i can definitely get the hype surrounding Cassie & Dean, though. that’s for sure.

all in all, i enjoyed Killer Instinct. the beginning may not have been super exciting, but like i said, it gets better eventually — and when it does... believe me, it’s impossible to put it down. i was left feeling extremely satisfied at the end.

another successful buddy read with my lovely charlotte. 💐 binging this series with you has been so much fun! <3

ᯓᡣ𐭩⋆°.⋆  "𝘐𝘵’𝘴 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘣𝘢𝘥 𝘮𝘦𝘮𝘰𝘳𝘪𝘦𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘵𝘦𝘢𝘳 𝘢 𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘴𝘰𝘯 𝘢𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘵. 𝘐𝘵’𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘨𝘰𝘰𝘥 𝘰𝘯𝘦𝘴."  ᯓᡣ𐭩⋆°.⋆

Nothing takes me out of a story like predicting plot twists in a thriller novel. I basically foresaw all of the twists and turns in this novel, yet I still kept reading in the hope of being mistaken. But, spoiler alert: I wasn't.

My expectations for this book were a little higher because I had heard from many readers that this series gets better with each book, but despite the first book being so slow, it was still far better than this one.

Despite being only 380 pages long, this book felt so extensive that I was at a loss for words. What are all these pages for? 75% of the novel is made up of the same repeating events, which left me feeling nothing but pure frustration. Considering the extremely slow pacing, this book might have easily been 150 pages short, or even better, a novella.

Speaking of our fmc Cassie Hobbes, I thought she was a great character in the first book, but her persona felt totally alien to me now. In contrast to the first book, she was blatantly obnoxious and incredibly self-centered in this one. I hated how she made everything about herself. Like get over it, girl—it's not all about you.

Lastly, despite the love triangle trope grating on my nerves, the only reason I'm giving this book an extra star is because cassie ended up with exactly who I wanted her to all along.

part of this review will have spoilers, but this first part will not.

: ̗̀➛ this series has managed to pull me in deeper with every single page. reading this book was a similar experience to the first one, absolutely captivated by the story and consuming every single word. the characters, their dynamics, the “you” chapters that let us inside the mind of the killer. there’s so many things that make this book so great. in my opinion, the key to a good book is making the readers invested in the characters, and I am SO incredibly invested.

: ̗̀➛ so first of all, the fact that there were three killers was actually shocking. the first one being the original suspect WAS ALSO CRAZY because we were led to believe that there was no possible way for him to be the killer. and then for the second killer to ALSO be “obvious” only to have an alibi?! I thought that these were misdirects, because that’s what they were painted out to be. I honestly really love the trope where a misdirect becomes a misdirect. the way JLB set up the whole killer thing was pretty cool honestly, the killers chose victims for each other so that people with motive would ALWAYS have an alibi. but after one of the killers gets killed, the question is, who’s doing the picking now?? MEANING THERES A THIRDDDD. and this was honestly so well done because if you really analyze it, the “you” POVs did feel different sometimes.

Cassie
╰┈➤ CASSIE THEY COULD NEVER MAKE ME HATE YOU. Cassie is the type of character that’ll make mistakes, but she’s the character that will actually own up to them. she’s different from the other naturals because she’s led by her emotions, she feels things more than the others. meaning she’ll put herself in harms way for the people she loves. but while she is the character that loves so much, she’s also the character that chooses who she loves wisely. when she’d first come to the naturals program she’d told the others in a game of truth or dare that she’s only loved one person. I HOPE we get a call back to that moment where the answer has completely changed because she’s found her new family. she’s just such a great main character and one of my favorite redheads.

Michael
╰┈➤ this is when I openly admit, team Michael. ya’ll really thought I was gonna pick the blond guy?! no thanks, double it and give it to the next person. let’s face the facts and admit this book wouldn’t be as good without Michael, they couldn’t have done it without HIM. no like actually tho. in the first book Michael full on got shot and then proceeded to save Cassie’s life, where was Dean might you ask? knocked tf out, lying on the floor. but that’s old news, Michael carried this book at the less exciting parts with his humor. whenever he was in a scene, I was absolutely laughing and having the time of my life. Lia
╰┈➤ I hated this girl in book one. but oh my god, I might be in the early stages of loving her character. she says it how it is, never holds back. and while this initially annoyed me beyond belief, I’ve grown to really enjoy her sassy bluntness. and now it’s time to be honest cassie and lia had the best dynamic in the book i mean come on, they go head to head the entirety of the first book and then in this one they end up eating ice cream on a roof while eavesdropping?! ˚୨୧⋆｡˚ ⋆ “𝘼 𝙥𝙧𝙤𝙛𝙞𝙡𝙚𝙧, 𝙖𝙣 𝙚𝙢𝙤𝙩𝙞𝙤𝙣 𝙧𝙚𝙖𝙙𝙚𝙧, 𝙖𝙣𝙙 𝙖 𝙡𝙞𝙚 𝙙𝙚𝙩𝙚𝙘𝙩𝙤𝙧 𝙬𝙚𝙣𝙩 𝙩𝙤 𝙖 𝙥𝙖𝙧𝙩𝙮”

CASSIE, MICHAEL, AND LIA ARE THE BEST TRIO. it’s like a black cat (Lia) a golden retriever (Michael) and an orange cat (Cassie) and I’m living for it like I live for the way these three interact. I was so giddy when they were working together.

˚୨୧⋆｡˚ ⋆ “𝙄 𝙩𝙖𝙠𝙚 𝙞𝙩 𝙮𝙤𝙪’𝙧𝙚 𝙈𝙞𝙘𝙝𝙖𝙚𝙡,” 𝙨𝙝𝙚 𝙨𝙖𝙞𝙙. “𝙏𝙝𝙚 𝙚𝙢𝙤𝙩𝙞𝙤𝙣 𝙧𝙚𝙖𝙙𝙚𝙧 𝙬𝙞𝙩𝙝 𝙩𝙝𝙚 𝙖𝙩𝙩𝙞𝙩𝙪𝙙𝙚 𝙥𝙧𝙤𝙗𝙡𝙚𝙢 𝙬𝙝𝙤’𝙨 𝙘𝙤𝙣𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙪𝙖𝙡𝙡𝙮 𝙙𝙤𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙨𝙩𝙪𝙥𝙞𝙙 𝙩𝙝𝙞𝙣𝙜𝙨 𝙛𝙤𝙧 𝙜𝙞𝙧𝙡𝙨.”

Sterling
╰┈➤ I HATED HER AT FIRST, AND I ADORED HER BY THE END. like actually, I loved her character so much more than I thought I would and more than that, I loved her relationship with Cassie. at first, Cassie was wary because of what happened with Locke, but by the end of the story it almost felt like Sterling mended the wound that Locke left on Cassie. I loved the way they could relate to each other. AND OH MY GOD, I literally gasped when it was revealed that Sterling was one of Redding’s (deans dad; serial killer) victims that got away. she was a big opening for deans backstory while also having her own character complexities and I love that.

in conclusion I loved this book. and while 1% of people have really made it to the end of this review, I could talk about the story for hours without getting bored. I absolutely recommend this series to anyone with a love for mystery, a bit of romance, and a nice found family.

edit because I genuinely can’t shut up about this
I wanna take a second to admire Jennifer’s ability to create complex characters with depth and detail while still managing to have so many. the biggest hit or miss when it comes to found families or friend groups like this is that sometimes there will be characters that lack the same emotional impact and complexities that other characters in the book may have. but all the main characters in this book felt equally dived into and I appreciate that so much.

══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══╡ Overview: ╞══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══

This book was half-half for me. Some parts were enjoyable, and some were very, very boring. It was longer than it should have been, in my opinion. I enjoyed book one more. Book 1 was faster-paced and more captivating for me to read, and I hoped the same for this book, too. I fear I was a bit disappointed, because I did expect this book to be better.

⁀જ➣꒰ ⋮ ρℓσт.꒱

I enjoyed the plot in this book, despite it being very boring at times. The pacing in this book was very slow. It felt like not much was happening for almost half of the book. I wasn't feeling the excitement I was feeling in the first book. However, once we got more action, I was on the edge of my seat and dying to read more of them.

That being said, the plot twists kept coming nonstop. There were several jaw-dropping moments in this book, and I was still shocked when I found out I was right about two plot twists. I don't like to predict plot twists cause it takes away from the reading experience for me. I was shocked, yes, but I thought I was going to be underwhelmed, until the plot twist that I never saw coming came.

⁀જ➣꒰⋮ 𝕽𝖔𝖒𝖆𝖓𝖈𝖊.꒱

I can’t begin to describe how much I hate the romance subplot in this book. It’s not even there. This entire book was focused on Dean, and Michael was just…there. I don’t get his purpose in making him a love interest. I sometimes even feel that Lia cares for Dean more than Cassie. I don’t know why the author wrote her this way, since it sometimes felt like Dean should end up with Lia and not Cassie. Am I saying I want that? Not at all, but the love triangle doesn’t make any sense if I’m not feeling any chemistry or tension between the characters. Wasn't a fan of this back-and-forth Cassie had going on, like bitch, just pick one, and don't lead on the one you won't pick.

⁀જ➣꒰⋮ ᭙𝕣ⅈ𝕥ⅈꪀᧁ.꒱

The writing in this book was, thankfully, better than the first book.

══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══╡ Characters: ╞══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══

This is the part where I get their actions, but I also don’t get it. There was a certain chapter in this book that made me want to pull my hair out—they were very childish. I get they’re teenagers, but I didn’t get their dumb argument where everyone was blaming the other.

I didn't like how Cassie told the FBI Agents where they were. I get why she did it, but I also don't. This book definitely made me realise I don’t miss being a teen at all. This book was just teens acting like teens (no offence, though 😂)

જ⁀➴ Cassie: She bothered me so much in this book. She was a bit stupid and reckless at times, and thought everything was about her. Like, hello? Calm down, girlie, please. She really needs to listen and learn how to follow rules, because she keeps getting herself in trouble 😭

જ⁀➴ Dean and Michael: I’m still on Dean’s team, but I couldn’t help but feel upset for Michael at the end. However, Michael definitely adds humour to the book. Dean is one of the sanest characters, despite his family history. I hated Dean’s dad so, so much. But I love that we got to see more of Dean's background and understand him more. While yes, Michael seems like the healthier option to choose, considering he is willing to acknowledge his feelings and wait for Cassie, I'm surprised to still be on Dean's team.

જ⁀➴ Sloane and Lia: I love Sloane so much. My heart broke for her when she felt excluded from the group. I love that she's self-aware of her shortcomings and that she cares so much for her friends. She just wants to be chosen, and that resonates with me so much. She and Dean are the sanest people in this book. I hated Lia in this book, too, but I did enjoy it when she was mean to Cassie when Cassie was bothering me.

જ⁀➴ Briggs, Veronica, and Judd: They are starting to grow on me.

── .✦ 𝓕𝓲𝓷𝓪𝓵 𝓣𝓱𝓸𝓾𝓰𝓱𝓽𝓼: This book had its ups and downs, but I’m still excited to continue the journey!

madi
408 reviews662 followers
March 4, 2025
This book had me obsessed from start to finish. The twists, the tension, the mind games—I couldn’t get enough. Jennifer Lynn Barnes somehow managed to make everything even darker and more intense than the first book, and I loved every second of it.

Cassie is stepping up in ways I didn’t expect. She’s still quiet and observant, but there’s a new kind of confidence in the way she approaches cases. She’s starting to understand her own abilities, but at the same time, she’s dealing with so much personal baggage. I love how she’s trying to find her place in this world of profiling and crime-solving, even when it pushes her way out of her comfort zone.

Dean was a lot in this one (in the best way). His story was brutal, and the way this case forced him to confront things he wanted to avoid made everything so much more personal. You can tell he’s trying to keep people at arm’s length, but the cracks in his walls? Yeah, they’re showing.

Michael is still the definition of trouble, but I can’t lie—he makes things interesting. He’s got this whole charming-but-infuriating thing down to a science, and the tension between him, Cassie, and Dean? Absolutely stressing me out.

At first, I didn’t really like Lia. She was a little too much, always messing with people and saying things just to get a reaction. But the more I got to know her, the more I realized there’s so much more to her. She’s smart, fearless, and scarily good at reading people. She plays things off like she doesn’t care, but when it really matters, you can tell she does. By the end of the book, she totally grew on me.

And then there’s Sloane, my favorite character ever . I knew I loved her before, but this book solidified it. She’s the kind of person who rattles off statistics like they’re casual conversation, drinks enough caffeine to power a small country, and somehow manages to be both the smartest and most unintentionally adorable person in the room. But beyond all the facts and quirks, there’s this quiet longing to be part of something—to be wanted—and that hit so hard. I want to wrap her in a blanket and tell her she’s the heart of this team. 💙

As for the mystery? Chilling. The way everything unraveled had me questioning everyone at some point, and just when I thought I knew where things were going, the book laughed in my face and flipped the script. That ending?? Yeah, I need the next book right now .

Except my package got delayed, so the third and fourth books aren’t even here yet. And now I have to reorder them, which means even more waiting. The universe is literally working against me. 😭

And before anyone calls me out, I know I’ve been reading this book for like a week, but that’s Pati’s fault—she’s made me addicted to The Rookie, and now my reading schedule is a disaster.

”some people said that broken bones grew back stronger. on the good days, i told myself that was true,

𓏲thoughts⸝ ⸝⸝

➵ i genuinely don’t know if i should scream, laugh, cry, jump, or all of the above. just know that this was absolutely phenomenal. if anyone doesn’t know, found family is my favourite tropes of all time, and this book?? oh my god it delivered. i love these characters and this world so much that it’s actually unhealthy to be as attached as i am. everything was just done so perfectly, and what can i say? in jennifer lynn barnes we trust.

we are once again following cassie as her journey continues in the naturals program. i think this book really steps the plot up compared to the first book. this one just felt darker from the beginning. there’s a new case that just pulls you in right away, this time having a connection to dean’s dad.

what i really liked is how the pacing almost never dragged. there was always something going on which is one of the aspects that made this book utterly unputdownable for the most part. there were times where i got a bit bored but it was honestly nothing too bad and it certainly didn’t last long either. the mystery in itself was so good and the plot twists genuinely had me putting a hand to my mouth.

as always, jennifer’s writing style remains one of my favourites. it’s so fast-paced and she manages to capture the characters’ voices so beautifully. the way cassie is described using her abilities feels believable and so does the way she observes the others using theirs. i really like how cassie’s voice stays just as consistent and thorough as in the first book. no, didn’t start casually trying to profile people after this book how could you think such a thing??

and can we just talk about the relationships between the main characters in this book?? gold. found family at it’s finest. the overprotective sibling dynamic between dean and lia had me smiling so hard. and i also loved how micheal was always the instigator trying to get a reaction out of dean whenever he could.


𓏲characters⸝ ⸝⸝
cassie hobbes‧˚₊⊹

she is honestly one of the smartest fmcs i’ve ever read about. the way she figures things out literally has me so jealous. like hello?? teach me your secrets please. also i learned so much from her. i literally try to apply her skills in my life because of how impressive they are. she is so loveable and sure, she makes some bad decisions but she gets back up and learns from them. seeing how her brain worked to solve cases had me so intrigued.

dean redding‧˚₊⊹

oh my baby. we learn more about his past in this book and let me just say i wanted to give him the biggest fucking hug throughout everything. he doesn’t deserve the father he got. the way he was described as the kid who was always smiling and so happy that everyone else was happy around him broke my heart. mostly because he always has his guard up now. i’m never getting over the he made me watch. i love him more than words can express.

cassie & dean‧˚₊⊹

yes, i am indeed team dean. i’m sorry, but they are soulmates in every lifetime and not even micheal can change that (i still love you micheal). everything about them together is so perfect and just makes sense i will never change my mind on that. i’m so excited to see more of them in the coming books.


𓏲quotes⸝ ⸝⸝

✧ ”most people built walls to protect themselves. dean did it to protect everyone else."

𓏲overall⸝ ⸝⸝

i went in with high expectations and i had them met. this book was almost as good as the first one and i’m so excited to continue this series. i definitely recommend it for all my fellow thriller lovers. this series so far is everything i could have imagined for it and more.

No dull moments. Not even one. 💜✨
This book had me hooked from page one — every chapter charged with tension, suspicion, and the constant question: who’s the killer this time?

The twists kept playing with my brain — I had so many theories (some right!), but just when I thought I cracked it, the story pulled me back with a “wait, what if…”

💔 Michael still owns my heart — charming, layered, and way more compelling than... well, Dean. Yeah, Cassie’s final choice? Not a fan. Dean feels dull and disappointing, though I get it — maybe she chose the one who mirrors her trauma best, and the one who shares her ability. His dark past definitely shaped who he is and explains a lot about his guarded nature. Still doesn’t mean I have to like it 😤

Lea? Iconic and entertaining as always 😎
Cassie? A total trouble magnet. Her ability helps, sure, but it’s often Sloane who saves the day with actual logic. I need more scenes for Sloane — she deserves the spotlight.

I loved this book. It was intense, clever, and filled with characters who are both brilliant and broken. I’m desperate to dive into the third one now — and honestly, it better live up to this or go even harder. I accept nothing less. 😁



Book two, here we go! Hoping for more twists, mind games, and murder. 💜👾
